items.title: Harold Dejan Interview, 1960-10-14
items.q: You said you played with Georgia Boyle.

ctx.x: What did he play? We played, we played tenor saxophone. And, we had to coach him to get up to take a course after he got the fright off him. He was tough, I'm telling you. And then he had McLaren, no time, no time, no time, I said a couple of months. He was sitting in the back of that plan and taking slow moves and things. Yeah, a couple of months. We had him at a bar on Brookhaven College, E.W. Brown. His daddy was over the Rabbitfoot Show one time. And Brookhaven, Brookhaven, a few miles from there, right in…
You said you played with Georgia Boyle.

Yeah, well, at the Willing, Georgia Boyle, you were there at the Willing. And, he said, now I'm going to take the Clarenor and the Luce when he fell out. And talk to you, like you holding a conversation there, and you want to take the Clarenor and the Luce, you know? And you can have a Spanish. Yeah, he was alright. He always had a terrible cough though. But he didn't. He could play it. Did he smoke? He was smoking. Oh, I know. He was smoking. Drink like that. Yeah. He had TB or anything, didn't he? Yeah, he…
